delete.description:
Delete an induced ontology and all its artifacts (graph triples,
vector embeddings, and registry entry) from a namespace.

Async — returns **202** immediately: the registry entry is removed
synchronously (so ``ListOntologies`` no longer lists it — the client-visible
status), then the slower Neptune named-graph DROP and per-embedding AOSS
teardown run in the background. Clients poll ``ListOntologies`` until the id
is gone. This mirrors the async accept flow and avoids the API Gateway 29s
integration timeout (504) on large ontologies.

The ontology id is a full IRI (contains ``://`` and ``#``), so it is passed
as a query parameter rather than a path label — API Gateway mangles a
URL-encoded ``#`` in a path segment (falls through to IAM auth → 403). This
mirrors the graph vertex-lookup endpoints (``/graph/class?uri=``).

parameters.description: Full IRI of the ontology to delete (passed as a query parameter).

post.description:
Repair malformed / mis-cased / aliased XSD datatype tokens in a proposal's
stored Turtle (e.g. `xsd:datetime` → `xsd:dateTime`, `xsd:varchar` →
`xsd:string`). User-initiated + consent-gated: the DatatypeTokenValidator
surfaces the offending tokens at validation time, and the user invokes this
to apply the fix. Server-authoritative (the canonical XSD map lives on the
server, not the client). Rewrites known-malformed tokens only — valid types
(incl. `xsd:date`) and unrecognized `xsd:` tokens are left untouched.

With `dryRun` true, computes and returns the same change list WITHOUT
persisting — used by the accept-time guard to detect unrepaired datatype
issues before an accept, without mutating the proposal.

post.description:
Approve all PENDING tables and columns of a DATABASE source asynchronously.

Returns 202 immediately and transitions the source's status to APPROVING.
A background worker writes DataZone asset revisions for any asset whose
review status actually changes. On completion the source's status becomes
APPROVED; on failure it becomes APPROVAL_FAILED. Clients poll the source's
status via GetSource until it leaves the APPROVING state.

Returns 409 if the source is not in PENDING_REVIEW or APPROVAL_FAILED.

CustomConnectorConfiguration.description:
Custom Athena Query Federation connector configuration — the
CUSTOM_CONNECTOR sub-type. The connector is a Lambda the customer authors
and deploys in their own account, which this service registers as a
Lambda-backed Athena data catalog in its own account; both discovery and
serve-time queries run through Athena against that catalog.

Unlike GlueConfiguration there is no Glue database behind the source, so
there is no catalogId and no cross-account IAM role to assume: the customer
grants access on the connector Lambda's own resource policy instead. There
is also no region member — the connector must live in this deployment's
region (see connectorFunctionArn).

connectorFunctionArn.description:
ARN of the connector Lambda. ONE Lambda serves both metadata and record
requests — what Athena calls a composite handler. The ARN's region must
equal this deployment's own region, because Athena can only invoke a
data-source connector co-located with the query.

Athena also accepts a split metadata/record PAIR of Lambdas, which this
member was once one half of. The pair is deliberately not modelled: the
reference connector and the CDK template customers are given both deploy a
single composite Lambda, so a second ARN asked every customer to reason
about a distinction almost none of them would make — and an ARN placed in
the wrong one of two adjacent members fails at query time rather than at
onboarding. Restoring it is purely additive (one optional member, plus the
record-function catalog parameter) if a customer ever needs the split form.

databaseName.description:
The single database inside the connector's catalog that this source
exposes. Exactly one database is resolved per source, so a connector
serving several databases is onboarded once per database.

tableFilter.description:
Include-filter applied to table names within databaseName. Omit to
discover every table.

tableExcludeFilter.description:
Exclude-filter applied to table names within databaseName, evaluated
after tableFilter.

DatabaseEngine.description: Database engine type for JDBC connections.

metadataEnrichmentEnabled.description:
Whether AI-powered business metadata enrichment runs for this source.
Set at creation time and persisted with the source record. When false
the scan pipeline skips the enrichment step and the source transitions
from SCANNING straight to PENDING_REVIEW.

tablesDiscovered.description: Number of tables discovered in the most recent scan.

lastScanJobId.description: Identifier of the most recent scan job.

lastScanAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent scan.

glueConnectionName.description:
Name of the Glue Connection that backs Athena federated queries
for this data source. Read-only and system-managed: populated
only for JDBC sub-types (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redshift, Oracle, SQL
Server, Snowflake) on first scan and removed when the source is
deleted. Null for S3/Iceberg-backed Glue databases — those are
queried via Athena's native AwsDataCatalog.

To query the source via Athena, pair this with the namespace's
`athenaWorkgroupName` and the `athenaDataCatalogName` below. See
the Athena Queryability section of `packages/sources/README.md`
for examples.

athenaDataCatalogName.description:
Name of the Athena data catalog registered for this source. Read-only
and system-managed, derived from `{resource-prefix}ds_{sourceId}`. Null
for S3/Iceberg-backed Glue databases, which are queried through Athena's
native `AwsDataCatalog`.

The addressing differs by sub-type, because the two catalogs are not the
same kind of object:

- JDBC sub-types: a managed Glue federated catalog, NESTED under
  `AwsDataCatalog`, and equal to `glueConnectionName`. Query it as
  `AwsDataCatalog.<athenaDataCatalogName>.<schema>.<table>`.
- CUSTOM_CONNECTOR: a LAMBDA-type Athena catalog bound to the customer's
  connector Lambda. It is a TOP-LEVEL catalog, not nested, so query it as
  `<athenaDataCatalogName>.<databaseName>.<table>`.

Run the query inside the namespace's Athena workgroup (see
NamespaceDetail.athenaWorkgroupName).

ProposalStatus.description:
Proposal status.

``inducing`` is the FIRST in-flight state: the induction was triggered and
a background worker is building the ontology. A stub proposal row is written
at trigger time (so the run is visible in the proposals list immediately and
survives a browser refresh); the same row is upserted to ``pending`` when the
worker finishes, or to ``failed`` if it errors. Clients poll ``ListProposals``
to observe the transition.

``accepting`` is a later in-flight state: the user submitted ``AcceptProposal``
and a background worker is merging the ontology. It is followed by
``embeddingsSync`` while the just-written embeddings become searchable in the
(eventually-consistent) vector index. The status then flips to ``accepted``
on success, or to ``acceptFailed`` with ``acceptError`` naming the pipeline
step that failed. An ``acceptFailed`` proposal is re-acceptable — the accept
pipeline is idempotent on re-run — so the client may submit
``AcceptProposal`` again once the cause is resolved. Clients poll
``GetProposal`` to observe the transitions.

VkgHealthStatus.description:
Health of the namespace's VKG translation service. HEALTHY: running and able
to translate. UNAVAILABLE: exists but not serving. PROVISIONING: service is
starting up (deployment in progress, not yet serving) — expected to become
HEALTHY shortly. UNKNOWN: not deployed yet or state undetermined.

ConfidenceScore.description:
A confidence score in [0, 1] for a query result, with an optional rationale
explaining how it was derived.

rationale.description: Explanation of how the score was derived.

ConformanceWarning.description:
A warning raised when a result row does not conform to the expected SHACL
shape, identifying the offending row and shape.

row.description: Index of the result row that failed conformance.

message.description: Human-readable description of the conformance warning.

DataSourceUnavailableErrorResponseConten.description:
Returned with HTTP 502 when a backing data source cannot be reached to
answer the query; `dataSourceId` identifies the unavailable source.

dataSourceId.description: Identifier of the data source that could not be reached.

classes.description: The classes in the namespace's schema.

DimensionFilter.description:
A filter constraining a query to rows matching a dimension value, with an
optional comparison operator (defaults to equality).

Server-side invariants NOT expressible as Smithy traits, enforced at
validation (a violation is a 400, see the Context Manager's InvokeRequest):
  - `name` must be non-blank, and is trimmed before use.
  - `name` is matched case-insensitively, and must be UNIQUE across the list —
    a mapping cannot express two values for one dimension. (`@uniqueItems`
    would not capture this: it compares whole structures, so two filters on
    the same name with different values would still pass.)
  - every filter must be applicable by the resolved metric; a filter the
    metric cannot apply fails closed rather than being dropped.

name.description: Name of the dimension to filter on.

value.description: Value to match for the dimension.

DimensionInfo.description:
A dimension a metric can be sliced by, with its name and type (e.g. time,
category).

type.description: Type of the dimension (e.g. time, category).

DimensionOperator.description:
Comparison operator applied by a DimensionFilter.

Equality is the only supported comparison: Tier-1 binds the value as a bare
SQL literal into a governed metric's template, which expresses `=` and nothing
else. Declared as an enum rather than a free-form String so a client asking
for an unsupported comparison is rejected by the contract instead of having it
silently applied as equality — a wrong answer returned with a 200.

Entity.description:
An entity (graph node) with its IRI, human-readable label, optional type, and
arbitrary properties.

type.description: Type (class IRI) of the entity, if known.

GraphContext.description:
Graph context accompanying an answer: the entities and relationships that
were traversed or cited.

entities.description: Entities traversed or cited for the answer.

relationships.description: Relationships traversed or cited for the answer.

startUri.description: IRI of the entity to start traversal from.

maxDepth.description: Maximum traversal depth from the starting entity.

relationshipFilter.description: Restrict traversal to these relationship (predicate) IRIs.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of entities to return.

topK.description: Maximum number of chunks to return.

minScore.description: Minimum relevance score a chunk must meet to be returned.

sourceFilter.description: Restrict results to these source document identifiers.

entityFilter.description: Restrict results to chunks annotated with these entities.

chunks.description: Ranked supporting chunks matching the query.

queryEmbeddingModel.description: Identifier of the embedding model used for the query.

MetricSummary.description:
A queryable metric with its identifier, name, description, dimensions,
synonyms, and backing data source.

dimensions.description: Dimensions the metric can be sliced by.

dataSourceId.description: Identifier of the data source backing the metric.

NamespaceNotFoundErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 404 when the target namespace does not exist or is not
visible to the caller.

namespaceId.description: Identifier of the namespace that was not found.

NoResultErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 404 when a pinned tier produced no data for the query —
a "no results" outcome rather than a server error.

tier.description: Pinned tier that produced no result (1 = metric match, 2 = structured query).

OntologyNotPublishedErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 409 when the namespace has no published ontology, so the
query cannot be resolved against a schema yet.

namespaceId.description: Identifier of the namespace whose ontology is not published.

detail.description: Additional detail about why the ontology is unavailable.

execute.description: Whether to execute the generated query (versus translate only).

tierOverride.description: Pin resolution to a specific tier, bypassing automatic routing.

mode.description:
Execution mode: "standard" (single-shot) or "deep-reasoning" (multi-step
reasoning loop). Orthogonal to the tier cascade. Absent = the serve
deployment default. Deep reasoning is higher-recall but much slower
(p50 ~90s), so a caller behind a short client timeout should send
"standard". "agentic" is the deprecated pre-rename spelling of
"deep-reasoning" and is still accepted.

dimensions.description: Dimension filters to constrain the query.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for the query, in milliseconds.

includeSupporting.description: Whether to include supporting content in the response.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of result rows to return.

requestId.description: Identifier of the request, for tracing and support.

sessionId.description: Identifier of the session the request belongs to.

QueryResult.description:
The top-level result of a query: the answering tier, confidence, tabular
rows and/or a synthesized answer, the query that ran, supporting content,
graph context, and an execution trace.

tier.description: The answering tier that produced this result.

resultRows.description: Tabular result rows returned by the query.

synthesizedAnswer.description: Natural-language answer synthesized from the results.

queryUsed.description: The query that was executed to produce the result.

sparqlGenerated.description: The SPARQL query generated for the result, if any.

trace.description: Step-by-step execution trace of the query.

ontologyVersion.description: Version of the ontology the query ran against.

dataSources.description: Identifiers of the data sources that contributed to the result.

QueryTranslationErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 400 when a natural-language question cannot be translated
into an executable query against the ontology.

detail.description: Additional detail about the translation failure.

RateLimitExceededErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 429 when the caller exceeds the request rate limit;
`retryAfterSeconds` indicates how long to wait before retrying.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying the request.

Relationship.description:
A directed relationship between two entities, identified by source, predicate,
and target IRIs.

predicateUri.description: IRI of the predicate linking source to target.

SchemaClass.description:
A class in the namespace's queryable schema, with its IRI, label, optional
description, properties, and parent class.

parentClass.description: IRI of the parent class, if any.

SchemaProperty.description:
A property of a schema class, with its IRI, label, value range (datatype or
target class), and optional description.

range.description: Value range of the property (datatype or target class).

metrics.description: The metrics available in the namespace.

nextToken.description: Pagination token for retrieving the next page, if any.

SupportingContent.description:
A knowledge-base chunk that supports an answer, with its text, source
document provenance, and relevance score.

sourceDocumentId.description: Identifier of the source document the chunk came from.

sourceDocumentName.description: Human-readable name of the source document.

relevanceScore.description: Relevance score of the chunk to the query.

TraceStep.description:
One step in a query's execution trace, recording what ran, its status,
timing, and any tool used or conformance warnings raised.

status.description: Status of the step (e.g. success or failure).

durationMs.description: Duration of the step in milliseconds.

toolUsed.description: Name of the tool invoked during the step, if any.

parallelGroup.description: Identifier of the parallel group this step ran in, if any.

wallMs.description: Wall-clock time for the step in milliseconds.

conformanceWarnings.description: Conformance warnings raised during the step.

query.description: Natural-language question to translate into SPARQL.

sparqlQuery.description: The SPARQL query generated from the question.

ontologyVersion.description: Version of the ontology the query was generated against.

TraversalDirection.description: Direction to follow relationships when traversing the graph.
